notes:
Lead profile: small legaltech startup building a conversational assistant for contract triage and document search. Inbound self-serve signup, experimented with embeddings + semantic search. Primary contact: Maya Torres (CTO); procurement/legal: Jordan Park.

Key asks from security questionnaire: SOC2 Type II evidence, canonical list of sub-processors (cloud provider, monitoring, analytics providers), standard DPA to review, details on encryption-at-rest and transit, retention and ability to delete customer data on request. They flagged third-party telemetry/analytics as a blocker.

What they told us (paraphrase / quotes):
- "We can do a small pilot on hosted API but legal needs SOC2 evidence before we commit to paid." — Maya (CTO)
- "If vendor can't produce a DPA and sub-processor list quickly, procurement won't approve in Q2." — Jordan (Procurement)

Technical constraints / preferences: mostly public cloud usage; low-latency (<200ms for single-turn search), throughput modest (5–10 rps during pilot). Cost sensitivity: SMB budget, looking to keep monthly spend < $3k for pilot. Model preferences: open-model variants welcome; prefer ability to pin model versions for consistency. Routing/fallback: not a priority for pilot, may want basic fallback to smaller model for cost control.

Action history and notes: AE provided links to pricing deck and quickstart. SE ran a short demo of embeddings pipeline and shared sample prompt sets. Legal submitted a 3-page vendor security questionnaire and requested a scanned SOC2 report or summary and DPA template. We logged a support ticket (INF-3241) to collate security artifacts.

Next steps (short):
- AE (Ethan) to attach Redwood SOC2 summary + SOC2 letter and canonical sub-processor list to Drive (by 2026-03-14).
- SE (Harper) to run 30m security Q&A w/ CTO (Maya) to answer tech details (2026-03-16 proposed).
- Send DPA template and ask legal for redlines; aim to close procurement in May (2026-05).

Sticking points: timing on SOC2 artifacts (they want Type II), DPA negotiation timeline, EU data residency note in questionnaire — they want confirmation that EU customer data can be restricted to EU region if needed in a future contract.

Notes on tone: conversational but risk-averse customer; SMB sizing means limited legal bandwidth but clear checklist-driven requirements. Keep responses short and attach single-document security bundle to reduce back-and-forth.
notes_summary: SMB legaltech inbound lead. Self-serve trial. Key blockers: SOC2 Type II, DPA, sub-processor list, EU data residency clarification. Next: send SOC2 summary, sub-processor list, DPA template, schedule security Q&A.
